A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAP-Net and UniMM-HAR research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and matchable despite pagination and supplementary numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition experiments and component ablations in Section 5, plus hyperparameter, efficiency, cross-source, and visualization results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results, including DAP-Net's UniMM-HAR accuracies in Table 3 and the additional evaluations in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the same DGR, DSQ, TMPD, MFR, backbone, and TAM procedures, including Doppler-guided densification, feature recalibration, text alignment, and cross-entropy training.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same UniMM-HAR data assembled from RadHAR, mRI, and MM-Fi. Cross-subject, cross-set, and the nine-action unseen-source evaluation in Appendix D.3 are retained without added datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same ten comparison methods, and the backbone, densification, and text-encoder comparisons retain their participants. Newly cited methods such as RadarLLM are not added to the reported experiments.

E3.justification: The splits and testing procedures in Section 3.3 and Appendices A.3/D.3 are unchanged. Both retain the same preprocessing, metrics, 150-epoch training budget, batch size, and model configurations.

E4.justification: The component, quantile, densification, prompt, and backbone ablations remain unchanged. Appendices B–D retain the same heterogeneity analyses, Doppler analyses, hyperparameter studies, efficiency comparisons, and attention visualizations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated training runs, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing descriptive statistics, including point-count standard deviations in v1 Table 14 and v2 Table S5, are unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched tables and figures retain their numerical results and findings. For example, Table 3 reports DAP-Net at 80.72% C-Sub and 81.82% C-Set in both versions; appendix sensitivity, efficiency, and cross-source results also match.

T1.justification: Equations 1–18 retain the same method definitions, radar-physics relationships, and evaluation formulas. No assumptions, derivations, proofs, or formal properties are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about UniMM-HAR's scale and heterogeneous coverage, DAP-Net's components, and recognition and cross-source performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of Doppler consistency, complementary module benefits, and source alignment are retained. Appendix discussions of radial-only velocity measurement and excessive densification's redundancy/noise tradeoffs are also unchanged.

D1.justification: GPU hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, data formats, and naming conventions are unchanged. Both versions provide the same code/dataset availability statement and repository link.

R1.justification: v2 adds eight cited works, including RadarLLM, mmBody, and Guo et al.'s radar Point Transformer study, and removes Tian et al.'s From Range-Angle Maps to Poses reference. Missing citations in Sections 2.2–2.3 are resolved, while the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 expands author affiliations, adds author identifiers, revises the introduction's opening motivation, and condenses Section 2.2. Bibliographic formatting is standardized, but the main section sequence and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 uses a larger page canvas with wider margins, relocates Tables 4–5 from page 13 to page 12, and reflows several appendix figures. Supplementary figures and tables receive S-prefixed labels; their designs and scientific content are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces unresolved citation placeholders in Sections 2.2–2.3 with identifiable references and tightens the related-work prose, improving traceability and clarity. The methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited to editorial quality.
